articles.title: Jay Horwitz: The 2001 Mets have always made good on the promise to ‘never forget’
articles.summary: BY JAY HORWITZ It’s just two words: “Never Forget.” For a quarter of a century now, that phrase has been the mantra of the 2001 Mets who helped the city heal...
articles.body:
It's just two words: "Never Forget." For a quarter of a century now, that phrase has been the mantra of the 2001 Mets who helped the city heal after 9/11.

Those players have done everything possible to keep alive the memories of those 2,977 people who died that September day.

Now, 25 years later, the nucleus of that team is still heavily involved in anniversary events this month.

On Sept. 8, there will be a firehouse visit to Ladder 25, Division 3 in Manhattan. Two days later, the guys will gather at Citi Field to watch the debut of Todd Zeile's film "When America Took the Field." Then, on 9/11, they will return to Citi to participate in MLB's Baseball Meal Pack.

In attendance for most of those events will be Mike Piazza, Al Leiter, John Franco, Robin Ventura and Zeile. David Wright will be there, too. David has never missed a firehouse visit when he is in New York. In my mind, he is an honorary 2001 Met.

I have been doing Mets public relations for a long time, 46 years to be exact. I am often asked who my favorite player was, and what team was my favorite. I am reluctant to answer because I don't want to offend anyone. Let me say this: The 2001 Mets were the right team for the right time.

None of us had experienced anything like this before. Thousands of people had died. No one knew what to expect. There was a stoppage of play. When would we continue to play, would there be a follow-up attack?

Our guys met every challenge and then some. We had local players who took what happened personally. Leiter was born in New Jersey. Franco came from Brooklyn and Staten Island, and Bobby Valentine was born in Connecticut. Then we had a group of veterans who just "Got It." Piazza, Ventura, Zeile, Joe McEwing, Vance Wilson, Glendon Rusch, Jay Payton and Edgardo Alfonzo all stepped to the forefront.

There were countless visits to Ground Zero. There wasn't a charity dinner or hospital visit that we didn't make. No arms were twisted either.

We have tried to come together each September to make a firehouse visit to pay our respects to the 343 firemen who passed away. All of us still shed a tear when we walk into a house and see plaques honoring the men who were killed in the attacks. These kinds of visits keep us connected and help us to not lose track of our goal to "Never Forget."

We were in Pittsburgh on Sept. 11, 2001. I can still remember watching the "Today" show when the planes hit The Towers. At first, you thought this might be an accident but then you quickly knew that this was no accident.

Our hotel was next to a federal building, so we had to move to the suburbs for safety. We stayed in a small hotel next to Robert Morris University. Two days later, we bused back home. It took us 10 hours. I remember crossing the George Washington Bridge, and Todd pointed out that there was only smoke where the Towers used to be.

As we made our way to Queens, there was dead silence the rest of the way. None of us knew what would happen next.

What happened next was that half of the Shea parking lot was turned into a recovery area. It was originally supposed to be used as a morgue, but so few bodies were recovered from the Towers that plans were switched.

Bobby V, Sue Lucchi and Kevin McCarthy of our Stadium Ops. department ran the area. We received supplies from all over the east coast. People came from Maryland, Ohio, and Upstate to drop off food, medical supplies and clothing.

We had a routine. In the mornings, we would work out but in the afternoons all of our players and staff packed trucks to send down to Ground Zero.

We kept the parking lot open until we started to play again. Sue maybe slept a few hours a night during that period. When she did sleep, it was on a cot at Shea. You can't forget about Mike Landeen who worked for Aramark at the time. He would stay there nightly and barbecue for the first responders.

I have to say a special word about Bobby. He was like a man possessed. He had two jobs, being our manager and making sure the trucks were packed. One of his best friends had jumped from one of the Towers and his death deeply affected him. Bobby had a restaurant back then and he fed all the workers on a daily basis.

Another thing we did during this time was make huge donations to Rusty Staub's New York Police and Fire Widows' & Children's Benefit Fund. Each member of our team gave a day's pay to the foundation.

During our workouts, our owner Fred Wilpon met with city officials to decide when we should play. It was decided that we would host the first game back on Sept. 21 vs. the Braves.

Before that we went to play a three-game series in Pittsburgh. I don't know how Bobby did it, but despite all that was going on, we were still in a pennant race.

We had a meeting with our ownership on the day of the game. Honestly, so many of us had mixed feelings about playing. Was it too early? How could baseball matter with all that went on in the world?

Twenty-five years later, I am still so proud that I was a part of the first sporting event played in NYC after the attacks. We needed to show the world that it was OK to smile and laugh again, and our game was the first step in that process.

I still recall every detail of that historic evening. You have to start with the Piazza home run which brought tears to everyone at Shea. I admit I was crying in the press box. One thing about Mike, he never wanted to be called a hero. In the weeks after he turned down numerous attempts to put him on the cover of various magazines.

Then there were the bag pipes, the color guards, the 21-gun salutes and the messages of hope from our players on the scoreboard.

I can still see two teams, who did not like each other, embracing mid-field.

I can still hear Diana Ross singing "God Bless America," Marc Anthony doing the "Star Spangled Banner," and Liza Minnelli giving a rousing rendition of "New York, New York" during the seventh-inning stretch. After she was done, she walked over and embraced Jay Payton, who was in the on-deck circle.

Our team did so many good things. We became the first club to wear special hats to honor the agencies who lost someone on 9/11. We were only supposed to wear those hats for a game or two, but we defied MLB and wore them for the rest of the year.

We were the first team to work with Tuesday's Children (now Tuesday's Promise), an organization that took care of the more than 3,000 kids who lost a parent.

I vividly recall our players signing autographs for the first responders in the dugout after we won. It was there I first met Carol Gies and here three sons who went on to become firefighters just like their late father Ronnie.

We were in uncharted waters back then. No sports team faced the challenges that we did. We passed every test with flying colors. Through the years we have never deviated from the words that have bonded us together: "Never Forget."

articles.title: Chelsea could welcome injured key players back against Arsenal
articles.summary: Chelsea take on Arsenal in the Premier League this weekend, and the Blues could welcome Moises Caicedo back into their squad for the game.The midfielder is o...
articles.body:
Chelsea take on Arsenal in the Premier League this weekend , and the Blues could welcome Moises Caicedo back into their squad for the game.

The midfielder is one of the most important players in the Chelsea team and will always start matches when fit. However, the Ecuador star has missed two of Chelsea's three competitive games this season because of injury.

Caicedo played a few minutes in their last match, but he is still being hampered by the same fitness problem. With the Arsenal game approaching, it remains uncertain whether he will be fit enough to get meaningful game time.

The Gunners are one of the teams to beat as they look to retain the league title they won last season. Chelsea will therefore be keen to make headlines by becoming the first team to beat Arsenal this term.

Caicedo is regarded as one of the best midfielders in Europe, so when he is available, he will always be expected to play. His presence in the middle of the pitch can give Chelsea greater control and improve their chances of getting a positive result.

However, Chelsea cannot afford to take unnecessary risks with the midfielder. His recent injury problem has already limited his involvement, and the Blues will need to be certain that he is ready before deciding whether to use him against Arsenal.

The match represents a major test for Xabi Alonso and his players. Chelsea have started the season well, but facing Arsenal will provide a clearer indication of how they can compete against the strongest team in the league.

Ahead of the game against Arsenal, Alonso was asked about Caicedo's fitness and explained that a final decision would be made after another assessment.

'We will check tomorrow. Tomorrow is the last decision for the squad on Sunday

'We need to not be worried. These things can happen and we need to check. Tomorrow we will make the final decision.'

Chelsea will therefore wait before confirming whether Caicedo can feature. The Blues will hope their key midfielder is available, but his fitness will be assessed carefully before the final decision is made.

articles.title: Predicting the New York Jets Opening Day Lineup
articles.summary: Who will start for the Jets?
articles.body:
We're finally back. New York Jets football is about a week away. Gang Green returns to the field with higher expectations than they've had in the past. That's not to say that anyone expects them to be a good football team, but they do have some expectations.

With Frank Reich leading the offense, and a talented Offensive Line and group of skill position players, the Jets offense should be fun for the first time in a long time. The Jets have not had an offense ranked outside the bottom-10 in scoring in the league since 2015. While the offense certainly won't compete with the best in the league, avoiding a bottom 10 mark in the league feels like it should be very attainable for this group.

Meanwhile, the Jets focus this offseason was almost all on the defensive side. Head Coach Aaron Glenn is going to call plays again, after yielding that responsibility in his first year. The Jets spent nearly all of their money in free agency on the defensive side of the ball. Not to mention they used the #2 pick and a 2nd round pick on premium defensive positions. Neither Glenn nor General Manager Darren Mougey can afford for the defense to be anything near as bad as it was last season.

So who are the players that will lead this team with modest expectations? Let's take a look at the expected starting lineup in Week 1 agains the Tennessee Titans.

The former Jets second round pick is back for his second stint with the franchise. Smith found success as a starter in his career with the Seahawks, but a disastrous stint last year with the Las Vegas Raiders left many speculating that the soon to be 36-year old quarterback is at the end of his career.

However, Smith dealt with a horrible situation last year. He had Chip Kelly as his offensive coordinator, the NFL's fifth-worst pass blocking offensive line, per PFF grade, arguably the NFL's worst WR group, and a severely unperforming top-10 pick in Ashton Jeanty at RB.

Smith comes into a much better situation here with Reich as his offensive coordinator, an above average OL, an above average RB, and a WR room that if nothing else has a true WR1. Will that be enough to get him back to how he looked in Seattle? I Ccn't say for sure, but Aaron Glenn is certainly betting on it.

Breece Hall needs no introduction. He's one of the best skill position players in Jets history. He's second in team history in yards from scrimmage per game, behind only Hall of Famer Curtis Martin. He averages over 1,500 yards per 17 games. He's a threat both in the backfield and as a receiver. He's a home run hitter, even if he may not be the most efficient runner in the league. If the Jets offense is going to take off this year, Hall will be a big reason for it.

One thing to keep an eye on though is how often Hall is used in the passing game. The last two Jets offensive coordinators underutilized Hall, only to admit that was a mistake as the season went on. Hall hasn't featured much in the passing game in practice this year with Smith only targeting him three times all camp according to Zack Rosenblatt .

Garrett Wilson is a true WR1 in this league. He suffered from injuries last season that limited him to by far the worst season of his career. He's an easy bounceback candidate for the Jets.

AD Mitchell is someone the Jets are incredibly high on. Reports all offseason have come that Mitchell and Smith have great chemsitry that could turn into a breakout season for the former second round pick. However, Mitchell is very unproven entering his third year.

I'm going with Isaiah Williams as the expected starter in the slot. He had a better camp and better preseason than Omar Cooper. Williams was also named a team captain. That said, I'd expect Cooper to get a ton of reps, and I wouldn't be surprised if he does in fact start over Williams.

Mason Taylor had a great camp and preseason, really establishing himself as Smith's safety blanket. Look for Taylor to be Smith's first option on short yardage plays and against zone. He's got great hands and finds soft spots in the defense easily. He just lacks the athleticism to be anything more.

That's where Kenyon Sadiq comes in, who likely would have been the opening day starter had he been healthy. However, he missed all of the offseason and camp due to injury after hernia surgery. It looks like he's going to be ready to take the field to start the season, as he's been practicing ahead of the game. However, that missed time is going to be hard to make up. Expect a slow start from the rookie.

Olu Fashanu made a nice jump last year. He finished as the Jets best pass blocking offensive lineman per PFF grade. He still struggles in the run game, and that's where he needs to make a big improvement this season. Still, if he stagnates, at least the Jets can go to sleep at night knowing they have a legitmate left tackle. After all, Olu finished with a 69.2 grade last season, that was 17th among the left tackles who played at least 50% of their team's snaps. From Week 7 to the end of the year, Olu was 17th among all tackles in total grade.

Parham was the Jets lone starter on offense acquired via free agency. Signing a two year, $20 million contract this offseason, Parham steps in at LG to replace John Simpson. He was part of that horrible Raiders offensive line last season. He gave up six sacks, the second most of any guard in the NFL. His 63.5 grade was 32nd of the 61 guards who played at least 50% of their team snaps last year. The hope is that was a blip, as Parham was much better the year before when his 74.3 grade was 17th among all guards who played at least 50% of snaps.

Josh Myers returns as the center after a disappointing season in 2025. He was the clear weak link in the Jets offensive line, grading out as second worst center in the league to play at least 50% of snaps. He gave up the third most sacks and the third most pressures from the position, and he was among the worst run blockers. Jets are hoping for major improvement here.

Joe Tippmann was named a captain this season. He enters his second full season as a guard in the NFL. He struggled with the transition early last season, but came into his own as the season went on. From Weeks 10-18 last season, Tippmann was 10th among all guards in pass block grade. He was also called for just one penalty over the final six games of the season.

Armand Membou is the Jets most talented offensive lineman. A stud out of the gate, Membou was a league average right tackle as a rookie. He's shown again this offseason that he has the talent to be an All-Pro. The question for the second year man is if he can take that leap in real games this season.

David Bailey was a lock to be here as soon as the Jets used the second pick in this April's draft on him. The former Texas Tech superstar comes in with high expectations as a pass rusher, and he's looked every bit that good in camp. Bailey is going to need to prove his worth quickly, as his pass rushing skill is his only dominant skill. He has a known weakness against the run.

Opposite him will be free agent addition Kingsley Enagbare. The former Packer had a standout camp while Joseph Ossai was injured. As a result he has leapfrogged Will McDonald on the depth chart and likely earned the Week 1 start.

This will be the first time Enagbare is a starter in his NFL career. The most snaps he's ever played in a single season before is 509. He's been used as a heavy rotation player, but never the main guy. Over his career, Enagbare has just a 9.8% pressure rate, slightly below league average for an EDGE rusher. He'll be expected to set the edge as the run stuffer opposite Bailey. That's a role he's never really thrived in at this point in his career. Perhaps Glenn's system gets more out of him.

Will McDonald will see plenty of snaps as well. He's the team's designated pass rusher and will be set loose on every pass down this season.

There's going to be a heavy rotation here, but I expect Sweat and Phillips to get the majority of the reps.

Sweat comes from Tennessee via trade. He had a breakout 2025 season where he established himself as arguably the NFL's best nose tackle. Of players who took at least 350 snaps, Sweat's 83.3 Defense grade was 5th best among all Defensive Tackles. His 79.2 run defense grade was 4th best.

I'm going with Phillips here as the second starting defensive tackle over David Onyemata for a couple of reasons. First, Phillips was with the team last year and likely has a better grip on what Glenn wants. Second, he was named a team captain. Third, his run defense will be important on early downs.

Another triumphant return for the Jets, as Demario Davis is back for his third stint with the team. The man Rex Ryan once compared to Ray Lewis hasn't had the same career as the all-time great, but he has been one of the best linebackers of the last decade.

Davis, even as he's grown older, has shown to be one of the game's best linebackers. Of linebackers to play at least 50% of snaps, Davis was 5th in defense grade last season. He's come to New York to be the leader of this defense and fill the vacuum as the voice on the field that CJ Mosley left. Of course, as with any player in their age 37 season, a steep dropoff could happen at any moment. But for now, the Jets are hoping that Davis owns the role that he's excelled in for over a decade now.

Meanwhile, Jamien Sherwood is happy he doesn't have to fill that role. In his first season as a starter after a big contract extension, Sherwood failed to live up to the money and fill the role that Mosley left behind. Now back in his usual role, Glenn is hoping to see the Sherwood that the Jets got the two years prior playing next to Quincy Williams and CJ Mosley.

The Jets cornerback room is a concern to say the least.

Brandon Stephens is still one of the most confusing free agent signings I've ever seen the Jets make. He was among the worst corners in the league before they signed him. And now he's their cornerback #1 without much competition despite not playing well last season. Stephens gave up over 500 yards on over 67% completion and 8 TDs last season. From Week 10-18 last season, Stephens ranked 57th of 69 cornerbacks who played at least 50% of their team's coverage snaps in coverage grade.

It's too soon to judge AZ Thomas. The Jets 3rd round pick last season sat on the bench last season before the team traded away Sauce Gardner. He took over as a starter at that point, but got injured soon after. Over the three games Thomas did start he allowed just 5 receptions on 11 targets for 46 yards and 0 TDs. Those are good numbers, though his coverage grade was just a 47.3, in large part thanks to two costly penalties. He's going to get a shot to start this season. If he can show those raw numbers are real that'd be a huge win for the Jets.

Jarvis Brownlee will start the season as the slot cornerback, but it does feel like he's just holding the spot until rookie second round pick D'Angelo Ponds is ready to take over. Brownlee was arguably the worst slot cornerback in the NFL last season. After arriving from the Titans via trade, Brownlee took over as the starting slot corner until he got hurt. From Week 6-12, when he was a starter, he had the third worst coverage grade in the NFL.

This unit did not have an interception last season. It was the first time in NFL history that a defense has gone an entire season without an interception. With no changes to the cornerback lineup expected in Week 1, it's just hope that will change.

Minkah Fitzpatrick isn't the player that he once was, but he's still an above average safety. After a career revival in Mimai last season, the Jets acquired Fitzpatrick in a trade and paired him with former Dolphins coaches as his DC and his DB coach. So they're hoping to keep that momentum going.

One thing to keep an eye on is that they changed Minkah's usage pretty heavily last season. He was used a lot closer to the line of scrimmage, and especially as a slot corner last year. While I don't expect he'll be used that close to the LOS again this season, I would expect a lot of three safety looks with Minkah acting as a slot corner.

By all accounts Dane Belton won the starting safety job this offseason. We'll see if that holds true. Belton is a traditional strong safety type. He plays almost like another linebacker and has a nose for the football. After a breakout season for the Giants last year, Belton is hoping to build on that with the Jets.

Andre Cisco will also see plenty of time, whether that's starting next to Minkah or as a third safety to take the deep role when Minkah slides into the slot.

Grupe was the New Orleans Saints kicker in 2024, 2025, and the early part of the 2026 season. He was an above average kicker in 2025 when he hit 87.1% of his field goals. He's a sniper from long range, nailing 70.3% from 50+ in his career. He has been erratic from 30-49 though, missing 9 combined kicks from that range over the last three seasons.

That said, after struggling early with the Saints last season, Grupe found a home in Indianapolis. He was perfect for the Colts, hitting all 11 field goals he took including four of four from 50+. His season, and career, long was 60 yards.

By all accounts Grupe had an excellent camp for the Colts, but was just beat out by Spencer Shraeder after missing two of four field goal attempts in preseason. One was from 61 yards, the other from 36 yards, though he did also hit from 46 and 36 in the preseason finale.

Austin McNamara was robbed of an All-Pro selection last season and was without a doubt the best Jet last season. He returns at the one position the Jets can confidently say is a strength.

Last year's team MVP, Isaiah Williams was also robbed of an All-Pro spot. He led the NFL in punt return TDs and was an all-around special teams stud.

This will be year three as the Jets primary kick returner for Nwangwu. He's returned one for a touchdown in each of the last two seasons. Always a dangerous return man, it's just about staying healthy for the former All-Pro kick returner.

articles.title: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva has neutral athlete status revoked, AP source says
articles.summary: Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva has had her permission to compete internationally as a neutral athlete revoked, a person familiar with the situation tol...
articles.body:
DUESSELDORF, Germany (AP) — Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva has had her permission to compete internationally as a neutral athlete revoked, a person familiar with the situation told The Associated Press on Saturday.

The latest twist in Valieva's career comes more than four years after disputes about her positive test overshadowed the 2022 Beijing Olympics .

The person said that Valieva was initially granted neutral status under a new International Skating Union rule for this season which states that skaters from Russia and Belarus are "presumed eligible unless they fall within the disqualifying criteria."

That status was then withdrawn from Valieva over concerns about a potential breach of criteria preventing skaters from being granted neutral status if they have previously supported Russia's war in Ukraine, the person said.

The status has also been withdrawn from Russian men's skater Mark Kondratiuk, who was a teammate of Valieva at the 2022 Olympics, the person said.

The ISU is due to rule on appeals by both athletes by the middle of next week and if the decision remains unchanged, the athletes would be able to appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the person added.

The person did not want to be identified because the details of such cases are not typically released publicly.

The revocation of Valieva's status was first reported by Russian news media. Valieva has not commented on her status.

The ISU had barred skaters from Russia and its ally Belarus in 2022 following the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

It allowed a limited number to return for the Milan Cortina Olympics and a qualifying event last season. Two Russian figure skaters, Adeliia Petrosian and Petr Gumennik, competed at the Olympics but neither won a medal .

For this season, the ISU has not limited the number of places for neutral athletes and has introduced a presumption that they are eligible unless found not to be.

The ISU rules say skaters may be refused if they are serving with military or security forces, have previously participated in military operations against Ukraine or have "actively and publicly supported that war" since 2022.

Then aged 15, Valieva was at the center of a legal battle during the 2022 Beijing Games when a sample she gave two months earlier tested positive for the banned substance trimetazidine.

The revelation came after Valieva won team gold with other Russian skaters. She was later disqualified from that event, which upgraded the United States to gold . Valieva was a contender for the women's gold medal but placed fourth and was criticized rink-side by her coach, Eteri Tutberidze.

Valieva eventually served a ban which expired in December 2025 and she has since competed in Russian events .

Rules were later changed to raise the minimum age for skaters to 17 in time for the Milan Cortina Olympics earlier this year.

articles.title: Browns 2026 season: 5 reasons I’m excited, 3 reasons I’m concerned
articles.summary: Preparing for the 2026 Cleveland Browns season, a few reasons to be excited, a few concerns starting with HC Todd Monken
articles.body:
While my Ohio State Buckeyes get their season started on Saturday, our Cleveland Browns will have to wait a week and a day, while enjoying a few days off right now , to unveil the new team under HC Todd Monken. So many changes this offseason, starting with Monken in place of HC Kevin Stefanski and a very young roster .

A ton of proverbial ink has been spilled about the Browns quarterback position and the trade of DE Myles Garrett . The reality is that both of those things are probably the biggest storylines around the team and deserved the attention they received.

While we are ready to move forward with Cleveland's 2026 season, the decisions made this offseason undergird everyone's expectations. If Garrett were still on the team, a solid veteran was starting at quarterback, the two exciting rookie wide receivers were on another team, and/or a young, inexperienced head coach was hired, Browns fans and media might see things differently heading into Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

A list of a few things I'm excited about and concerned about:

While no one can say for certain whether Monken will be in over his head as a head coach, I have no doubt that he will not be embarrassing Browns fans. For the first time in a long time, Cleveland has a coach with a ton of experience all over the NFL and college. While he's a first-time head coach and could be fired within a year, I am confident he will not embarrass himself or the team, big picture.

Concerned that the stepdown from Garrett to Verse uncovers many defensive deficiencies

Garrett is the best player in the NFL, just ask the other players. His presence alone made Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Denzel Ward, Grant Delpit , and the rest of the defense better. Add on his performance, and it is possible that Browns defenders are not as good, and some may not even be close, as they've looked with Garrett with them. Verse is a darn good player, but the difference between good and game-changer can be stark.

Excited about KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston AND…

… Quinson Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr., and Isaiah Bond.

I'm not sure the last time Cleveland had five offensive weapons that have either proven they are good players or clearly have the ability to do so. Bond might be the least productive, but his high end speed will help open things up for the rest of the Browns offense. Concepcion and Boston can be used in a variety of ways and have already made a lot of plays to start their careers.

Just a lot of fun around a rebuilt offensive line and a mystery box of concern at quarterback.

Why wouldn't I be? Yes, an offense can be good running the ball and with a few key passes, but defenses that get to load the box can make things tough for Judkins and the rest of the running game. Whether it is Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , or Taylen Green, the Browns offense could be handicapped and impact the development of the young players if the quarterback play is as bad or worse than last year's.

Excited about what is next for Graham and Schwesinger

The Defensive Rookie of the Year outplayed Cleveland's top pick (Graham) last year, but the defensive tackle really improved as the year went on. Very excited to see how those two young guys, along with Verse, Maliek Collins , and Quincy Williams , perform in the front seven in Year 2.

The Browns have done very little, in fact, the opposite, to ingratiate themselves with the greatest fanbase in the world. The decision to start Watson added to that after his fan-blaming press conference, but Cleveland fans have slowly become apathetic toward their team. The Browns do not deserve support, but I am concerned that fans will miss out on the fun stuff because of the losing that has happened and could happen more this season.

Excited about the upside, development of the Browns roster

My favorite type of sports team is a championship-level team. After that is the young developing team with a lot of upside. Cleveland does not have the former but does have the latter, and I'm excited to share that with Browns fans who are able to push through even if the team is losing games. It really is one of the reasons I'm so excited for the SB Nation app, which I've said over and over again is all about bringing community together .

Getting to talk about how we see the offensive line coming together, how those weapons on offense are playing well together and off of each other, how the defense is more creative and versatile, how "EMan" (Emmanuel McNeil-Warren) is being used, and, yes, the 2027 NFL draft helping complete the three-year rebuild are all things that are better when we get to talk about them together.

I believe in the core of this team. I believe they have a chance to be decent to good this year, and I do believe they'll be a fringe playoff contender in 2027. There is a bunch to be excited about, but the obvious concerns still linger.

What are you excited about and concerned about heading into the 2026 Browns season?

articles.title: Liberty avenges 2025 loss to Utah power with comeback win
articles.summary: The Liberty Lions scored 24 unanswered points in a home win over Utah's Corner Canyon.
articles.body:
Early in the third quarter on Friday, Sept. 4, Draper (UT) Corner Canyon (3-1) was playing free and loose, and had host Peoria Liberty on the ropes for the second straight year.

That was until Liberty (2-0) got a spark in the form of sophomore quarterback Jason Haines, whose touchdown pass with 7:08 left in the quarter was the first of 24 unanswered points, as the host Lions defeated Corner Canyon, 38-14, on Friday, Sept. 4.

The win for Liberty avenged the 45-14 loss they suffered at the hands of Corner Canyon in Draper, Utah last season, which was the only regular-season loss for the Lions in 2025.

Corner Canyon built upon its momentum in the second half when Liberty fumbled the ball early in the third quarter deep in its own territory. The loose ball was scooped up by Corner Canyon's Ryce Palepoi. The senior then took it to the end zone for a touchdown, which gave the visitors a 24-14 lead, their biggest of the night.

It was at that point that Liberty (2-0) flipped a switch. The Lions responded by marching down the field in a drive capped by Haines' 31-yard touchdown pass to senior Carter Rothe, which cut the Corner Canyon lead to 24-21 and was the first of 24 unanswered points that eventually secured the win for Liberty.

Haines had his fingerprints all over the scoresheet for Liberty as he was responsible for four of his team's scores, including a 23-yard pass late in the first half to senior Braxton Huynh that tied the game following a successful two-point conversion. His lone rushing score on the night came on a two-yard quarterback keeper with 7:40 left in regulation that extended the Liberty lead to 31-24.

Corner Canyon's early momentum came thanks in large part to quarterback Jaxon Pehrson. The senior put his team on the scoreboard first courtesy of a 5-yard pass to Diesel Dort early in the second quarter. He gave his team a 14-6 advantage later that quarter when he connected with junior Beckam Coon on a 15-yard catch.

"It just shows that we're a really tough team to beat. Every week we're just going to keep getting better - starting tomorrow." - Liberty sophomore quarterback Jason Haines on the resiliency his team showed against Corner Canyon

"This game was hard. They do a lot defensively and bring a lot of pressure. So, we knew that was going to be a challenge … but he (Haines) did a good job fighting and clawing, and then guys made plays around him. We ran the ball really well tonight, too." - Liberty Head Coach Colin Thomas on Haines and the challenge he faced against Corner Canyon.

Liberty will be back in action Friday, Sept. 11, hosting Gilbert Highland.

articles.title: Former Sixers F ranked among greatest European players of all time

articles.body:
Toni Kukoc is known mostly for winning three championships alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen with the Chicago Bulls , along with drawing their ire in the Olympics, but for a brief moment, he played for the Philadelphia 76ers .

The Sixers acquired Kukoc from the Bulls at the 2000 deadline and he played 80 games for them before he was sent to the Atlanta Hawks at the 2001 deadline in the big Dikembe Mutombo deal. Overall, Kukoc averaged 9.8 points and 3.8 rebounds in Philadelphia.

HoopsHype ranked the top 50 European players of all time and Kukoc comes in ranked No. 14 on the list:

Toni Kukoc was a terrific all-around player, so crafty and smooth with the ball in his hands yet tenacious when he needed to be. Kukoc played a big role in three championship teams for the Bulls, though things didn't go so well when he was tasked with being the No. 1 guy post-Last Dance. You don't often see winning runs like the one he had between 1989 and 1998.

Kukoc is in the Hall of Fame after a terrific career with the Bulls, Sixers, Hawks, and Milwaukee Bucks. He won 6th Man of the Year in 1996 with Chicago.

articles.title: El coche más Temerario de la Policía italiana: un Lamborghini de 920 CV para salvar vidas
articles.standfirst: El cuerpo recibe una unidad del híbrido de casi 1.000 CV que se utilizará para labores médicas de emergencia
articles.summary: El cuerpo recibe una unidad del híbrido de casi 1.000 CV que se utilizará para labores médicas de emergencia
articles.body: Después de la Policía de Dubái, es la italiana, la Polizia di Stato, los que pueden presumir de una flota de coches (o, al menos, de algunas unidades) realmente especial. Algo que puede parecer lógico con marcas locales como Ferrari o Lamborghini que estarían encantadas de proveer a sus fuerzas del orden. No es el caso de los de Maranello, pero sí de los de Sant'Agata que ya llevan un tiempo colaborando con la Policía italiana (en concreto, desde el año 2004). El primero fue el Gallardo (y después el Gallardo LP 560-4), después llegaron los más recientes Huracán y hace poco también un Urus Performante. Los Carabinieri los han empleado mayoritariamente en misiones hospitalarias, como el transporte rápido de órganos para transplantes y material médico... y esa seguirá siendo su labor. Pero el tiempo pasa y la marca boloñesa renuva su gama de modelos... y con ella también la flota policial. De hecho, el cuerpo estatal acaba de mostrar el que será su séptimo coche patrulla con el escudo del toro en el frontal: nada menos que un espectacular Lamborghini Temerario. Se trata del modelo que sustituye al Huracán como el modelo central de la gama de Sant'Agata. Es un deportivo de nueva generación, con un motor híbrido que combina un V8 biturbo de combustión con tres propulsores eléctricos que entregan en total la friolera de 920 caballos de potencia. Mucho más que los 610 CV del Huracán y, sobre todo, es bastante más rápido ya que el Temerario supera los 340 km/h frente a los 325 km/h de su predecesor. Las imágenes de la Polizia muestran al Temerario personalizado con los colores del cuerpo (azul y blanco) con la bandera italiana en los lateralas. Para el interior, los Carabinieri han elegido el color chocolate para los tapizados. .La unidad del Temerario Polizia fue entregada a su nuevo dueño en una ceremonia celebrada en la propia fábrica de Sant'Agata Bolognese a la que acudió el presidente de la República Italiana, Matteo Piantedosi, y el CEO de Lamborghini, Stephan Winkelmann.

articles.title: Super League: Wakefield Trinity secure 25-18 victory over Warrington Wolves as battle for third spot rolls on
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity still have an outside chance of finishing in third spot in Super League; Warrington Wolves need to win in Round 27 to clinch it; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live
articles.body:
The win for Daryl Powell's side means they are still in with an outside chance of finishing third because the win moves them within two points of Warrington. The Wolves remain on 38 points and Wakefield are now on 36 in fourth spot.

Warrington, meanwhile, will need a win in Round 27 against Toulouse Olympique to wrap up third spot.

Warrington led 14-6 at half-time thanks to two Leon Hayes penalties and tries from Josh Smith and Matty Ashton, Hayes sending over the conversion for the second as the hooter went. Wakefield went over through Tom Johnstone and Max Jowitt added the extras.

Wakefield hit back in the second half as Isaiah Vagan found a double, Cam Scott went over and Mason Lino added a drop goal along with perfection off the tee from Max Jowitt.

That meant a solitary unconverted Albert Hopoate try was not enough for Warrington to hold on for the win.

An enthralling battle sees Wakefield come out on top

It was a battle between third and fourth and so attrition was expected to be the word of the day as these two teams tried to pick up a crucial two points in front of a packed out stadium.

That back-and-forth completion ensued early on as both sides traded territory and possession with minimal interference until the 10th minute when Hayes slotted over a penalty to put the visitors 2-0 up.

Another penalty followed just three minutes later for a late hit off the ball and Hayes duly obliged with the boot again to move the Wolves 4-0 up.

Once again, nothing could separate the two outfits until the 28th minute when Wakefield got a penalty, went through hands to the left, and Johnstone put the step on Josh Smith to go over. Jowitt converted to put Trinity 6-4 in front.

With just over five minutes remaining of the first 40, Warrington hit back. Some nice hands to the right, started by George Williams, saw Smith get one back on Johnstone for his earlier effort. Hayes could not convert from the touchline and so Warrington had a narrow 8-6 lead.

Burgess' side were not done there and with more territory, Williams put through an exceptional grubber which Ashton superbly jumped on in the corner. With that, and Hayes' conversion, Warrington led 14-6 at half-time.

Wakefield made sure to come back out in the second half and immediately put the pressure on as Vagana went over twice in quick succession, powering through a hole from close range on both occasions, the second time following a huge break downfield from Hall then Johnstone. Jowitt added the extra four points available to move Wakefield 18-14 ahead.

Warrington were not dismayed by the fight back and at the first chance of real pressure went over in the corner once again, this time through Hopoate but as Hayes skewed the conversion attempt, scores were level with a quarter of the game remaining.

The air was full of nerves from both sets of fans until the stadium erupted when Scott barrelled over off the back of a goal line dropout then set restart as Toby King was caught out, Jowitt continuing his perfection with the boot to put Trinity six points ahead with under 10 minutes remaining.

The Wolves chanced their arm but to no avail and with mistakes costing them key opportunities, Lino sent over the drop goal that confirmed they had succumbed to their seventh loss of the season.

articles.title: GOAT mindset? How Cristiano Ronaldo carries two distinct sides away from the public eye
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has two very different sides. A former team-mate has revealed what he is like when the cameras stop rolling.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has two very different sides. A former team-mate has revealed what he is like when the cameras stop rolling.

Alvaro Gonzalez played alongside Ronaldo at Al-Nassr during the 2022-23 campaign. Speaking to Radio MARCA, the ex-centre-back lifted the lid on the man behind the goals.

The answer depends on which Ronaldo you catch.

Gonzalez speaks out on the two sides of Cristiano Ronaldo

Inside the dressing room, Gonzalez says, Ronaldo is not the intense superstar the world expects.

"Honestly, and after confirming it with other team-mates we've had in common, he's absolutely fantastic inside the dressing room," Gonzalez said. "Inside the dressing room, he's a completely normal person, approachable and someone who helps you."

The moment he steps through the tunnel, though, everything changes.

"From the moment he leaves the dressing room and steps onto the pitch, he completely changes. He's a competitive beast," Gonzalez added.

"Afterwards, we'd go to the jacuzzi, have some laughs and joke around, and it would all be forgotten. People like him and [Lionel] Messi will go down in the history of football."

It is the same switch that has defined Ronaldo's two decades at the top. The ability to flip from relaxed team-mate to ruthless competitor in an instant.

The 41-year-old remains one of the best finishers in the world, having guided Al-Nassr to the Saudi Pro League title last season.

CR7 has recently hinted that this could probably be his last season as a professional football player.

That competitive edge is still pointed at history. Ronaldo, contracted to Al-Nassr until June 2027, is chasing 1,000 career goals, with 978 in 1,333 appearances for club and country.

The milestone hunt adds a new layer to every game, yet the man in the dressing room apparently stays the same.

His current boss shares the admiration. Ange Postecoglou has said being a small part of Ronaldo's story was part of the attraction of taking the Al-Nassr job.

"You find yourself thinking: I could become a small part of his story too," he said.

Two sides, one player, and a legacy already secure either way.

articles.title: Colston Loveland already sees growth in Bears rookie Dillon Thieneman
articles.summary: A key component of the Chicago Bears' defense in 2026 will be the development of Dillon Thieneman. Colston Loveland thinks he's well on his way.
articles.body:
As we creep ever closer to the start of the 2026 Chicago Bears season, questions persist about the state of their defense. One element of their roster that would go a long way toward quelling any existent concerns, though, is the ability on the part of Dillon Thieneman to develop quickly at the back of their secondary.

That the Bears were able to select Thieneman at the 25th spot of the 2026 NFL Draft read as something of a surprise due to projections that had him lingering more around the top 20. With the Bears letting each of Jaquan Brisker and Kevin Byard walk in free agency, however, they were pleased to be able to grab the former Oregon Duck at their original spot without needing to move.

The expectation was that Thieneman would form a new tandem at the safety position alongside Coby Bryant. With the latter now out for most of the season (if not the entirety of it), there is even more of an onus on the rookie to adjust to the top level as quickly as possible. If there's a positive to be found among such an urgent mindset, it's that the development he'll need to showcase is already beginning to manifest, at least in the eyes of tight end Colston Loveland.

Chicago Bears 53-man roster for 2026 season

"He's got a great routine," Loveland said. "I see him in the weight room before practice getting right, he does the same thing every single day. I got him a good amount early on, but he was always in position. By the end of camp, he started making plays on the ball. It was cool to see. He's a great player, super fast, physical, and he's grown so much throughout camp. I'm excited to see him go out there on Sundays."

It's difficult to overstate the value of confidence for a rookie. And what Loveland is describing what is being demonstrated by Thieneman certainly reads as an increase in just that. With his positioning being in place from the jump, the fact that he's reached the point of, in practice, becoming more attack-oriented speaks to a psychological growth that is paramount for rookies that are immediately thrust into a starting role.

If Loveland's observation is any indication, Thieneman is on track to demonstrate exactly the type of speedy development that the Bears are going to need out of him in 2026.

articles.title: ESPN insider reveals when Jets could start Cade Klubnik at QB during 2026 season
articles.summary: This potential Jets QB switch could come deep into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The New York Jets have a lot of new and exciting players on both sides of the ball to watch in 2026. While they might not be a playoff contender, this should be a much more entertaining season than what 2025 gave to Jets fans.

One of the big reasons why is Geno Smith being back as the starting quarterback. While he might not be anything great at this stage of his NFL career, he's much more exciting than Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, or Brady Cook.

But after him comes rookie fourth-rounder Cade Klubnik. He's the backup QB and is sure to see some game action this year. But when? According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , the Jets QB switch could come late in the year, possibly as late as December.

Jets could switch to Cade Klubnik as QB1 late in regular season

"If the Jets fall out of contention and/or Geno Smith struggles, Klubnik could get a late-season look," Graziano writes.

There's no guarantee the Jets will hand the keys to the offense over to Klubnik, but considering they have three first-round picks and are likely to take a QB in the 2027 NFL Draft, it would make sense to see what Klubnik can do.

If, somehow, Klubnik plays lights out to end the season, the Jets might be willing to use their first-round picks to fill out the rest of the roster to build around Klubnik. That's not likely, but they won't know if that's a path the Jets could take if he doesn't start.

But such a start for the rookie fourth-rounder, whom the Jets traded up to get, is likely to come late in the season. Graziano compared Klubnik to Arizona Cardinals rookie QB Carson Beck, who is potentially getting his first start in December.

That would mean Klubnik gets the start coming out of the bye week in Week 14, with matchups against the Denver Broncos , Cardinals, New England Patriots , Minnesota Vikings , and Buffalo Bills to close out the 2026 season.

It's not an easy schedule, but it's all the more reason to give Klubnik a chance to earn the long-term QB position. If he thrives in those games, he'll likely have proven he's worth investing in.

But if he struggles, then the Jets likely wind up with a top pick in the NFL Draft and use it to find their quarterback of the future.

Jets fans should not expect to see Klubnik until very late in the regular season, barring Smith getting hurt or playing too poorly to ignore. Still, the fourth-round rookie is likely to get at least some action, as the Jets really have nothing to lose.

articles.title: ‘Clout Chasing With Made Up Stories’ — Richard Sherman Calls Out Robert Griffin III for Spewing ‘Outright Lies’ About Stanford
articles.summary: Former NFL stars Robert Griffin III and Richard Sherman are going at it after Griffin alleged that Stanford used to pay players under the table. Sherman defe...
articles.body:
Former NFL stars Robert Griffin III and Richard Sherman are going at it after Griffin alleged that Stanford used to pay players under the table.

Sherman defended his alma mater and went after Griffin for his accusation, and the Heisman-Trophy winner refused to back down from his statement.

Richard Sherman Blasts Robert Griffin III for Accusing Stanford of Paying Players

This all started when Griffin appeared on "The Dan Patrick Show" and was asked which schools were known for paying players under the table prior to the NIL era.

Griffin stated that SEC schools paid the most, but alleged that Stanford and Florida State were also major offenders.

"I know for a fact that the SEC was paying the most under the table… There were two teams outside of the SEC that were paying a lot of guys under the table, and it was Stanford and Florida State," Griffin said. "You're talking hundreds of thousands per player. They were spending millions already back then, doing it in unique ways. I won't get into all of that; I'm not trying to get sued!"

He eventually added that some schools would set up bank accounts for certain players and deposit money into them, while also funneling money to players through internships.

Sherman wasn't thrilled to see Griffin accusing Stanford of breaking the rules. Stanford already had a tough night on Friday, with Miami blowing them out 45-6 in Week 1 behind a monster performance from stars Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah. Sherman didn't mince words while calling out Griffin for his allegations.

"I usually don't comment on what [Robert Griffin III] says but you aren't just going to disparage Stanford with outright lies. Stanford has never paid any players under the table and had no need to. Not sure what your issue is but the clout chasing with made up stories need to end," said Sherman .

Griffin's accusation wasn't limited to Stanford, but Sherman wasn't going to let it slide once his school was mentioned. Griffin refused to back down, responding to Sherman.

"Don't do this Richard. You comment when it's pro you and Stanford. Evidence below. I don't lie about any story I have shared. You may not have been paid and that's okay. But Stanford did pay some of their guys," said Griffin , while sharing a screenshot of a previous exchange with Sherman where he wrote, "What happens in P.A. stays in P.A."

Sherman seems adamant that his alma mater was not breaking the NCAA's rules by paying players, but Griffin is adamant that Stanford was throwing money around.

It's possible that Griffin is right and Sherman just wasn't aware that some of his teammates were getting paid, but it remains to be seen if this beef between two former NFL stars escalates.

articles.body:
Former Top Gear and The Grand Tour host Jeremy Clarkson has promised the whole Alpine Formula 1 team a Hawkstone beer if Pierre Gasly wins the Italian Grand Prix.

Gasly topped Saturday's qualifying session at Monza, securing his maiden pole position for Sunday's race.

Clarkson, whose Diddly Squat Farm in Chipping Norton is situated close to Alpine's Enstone headquarters, quickly reacted to the milestone moment. Posting on X, the Clarkson's Farm presenter made a public promise to the team.

"Right. Pierre Gasly. No pressure but if you translate that pole into a win, the whole team gets a Hawkstone. Go Chipping Norton team," he posted.

It continues a trend of Clarkson publicly backing his "local" F1 team. In the 2023 season, he tweeted during the Monaco Grand Prix that he would buy the entire Alpine team a pint if Esteban Ocon secured a podium finish. When Ocon successfully finished third, Clarkson honoured his end of the bargain. He personally drove his Lamborghini tractor to the Enstone factory, delivering a trailer laden with 1000 bottles of his Hawkstone beer to the staff.

Gasly's performance at Monza, the same circuit where he claimed his maiden grand prix victory for AlphaTauri in 2020, came as a shock in a season that has so far been dominated by Mercedes .

"I acquired a lot of emotions, so I'm just extremely happy for the whole team. I'm extremely happy with our performance. It's been nine years I'm in Formula 1, trying to give my best absolutely every single weekend," Gasly explained in the post-qualifying press conference.

"It's not every time we get a car to fight for pole position, and today it was the case. I'm really, really happy, really proud to have seized this chance and make it work. It was a heck of a lap.

"We've been on it since the first lap in Q1. It's been feeling good. I got my first win here in Monza, and now I get my first pole position, so definitely a special place to me."

articles.title: Ex-Dolphins DT Raekwon Davis arrested in Harris Co. after dispute over truck key
articles.summary: Court records say the case started with a replacement key issue at his Cypress home.
articles.body:
Former Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Raekwon Davis was arrested in Harris County after court records say a dispute over a replacement truck key allegedly ended with him choking a man and pointing a gun at him.

Davis, 29, was arrested Thursday and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon in the 338th District Court.

Davis was a second-round pick by the Miami Dolphins in the 2020 NFL Draft out of Alabama. After four seasons in South Beach, Davis jumped to the AFC South where he played for the Indianapolis Colts , Davis did not play in 2025 and has registered two career sacks across 80 career games and 48 starts.

Arrest paperwork said the entire incident began when the owner of a mobile vehicle detailing business told investigators one of his employees cleaned Davis' white Ford F-350 at Davis' Cypress home on August 29 and accidentally left the key inside a work van.

The victim told investigators he hired an Uber courier to bring the key back to Davis because he was working another job and was not near Davis. The courier dropped the key at a white truck, but court documents say Davis later texted the victim asking where the key was.

The victim then hired a locksmith to replace the key. Court documents say the victim and locksmith arrived at Davis' home around 6:30 p.m. Aug. 30, and the locksmith began working on the truck while the victim and Davis talked.

That is where the court record gets oddly specific.

"The locksmith began having issues with programming the key fob which caused the truck to not start," court documents said. "The locksmith exclaimed 'man f***!,' at which time [the victim] turned to Defendant and observed Defendant charging at [the victim] with both arms outstretched."

The victim told investigators Davis hit his chest "at force," backed him into a fence and caused him pain. Davis then allegedly pushed him to the ground, got on top of him and started choking him, according to the complaint.

"[The victim] advised that it was hard to [breathe] and he could barely speak while Defendant was squeezing his throat," the complaint states.

The complaint then says Davis then allegedly called out to someone living with him to get his gun. That person gave Davis a handgun, which the victim described as a "black glock," according to court records.

The victim told investigators Davis pointed the handgun at the locksmith and told him to "look away or keep working." Davis then allegedly moved the handgun back toward the victim, who interpreted it as a direct threat against his life, according to the complaint.

The victim said he was able to "successfully 'bucked' Defendant off of him," though he told investigators he was not sure if Davis was about to pistol-whip him or continue holding him at gunpoint, according to the arrest affidavit.

A Harris County magistrate found probable cause had previously been determined. A felony bail order filed Sept. 4 shows bail was temporarily denied pending a hearing, with personal bond marked "not eligible."

Chron has reached out to Davis' attorney for comment.

articles.title: Watch Jim Tressel honored with Ohio Stadium Ring of Honor ceremony
articles.summary: Former Ohio State coach Jim Tressel was honored with a spot in the Ohio Stadium Ring of Honor during the season opener.
articles.body:
Former Ohio State football coach Jim Tressel was enshrined in the Ohio State Ring of Honor during the Buckeyes season opener Sept. 5 , with permanent signage next to Woody Hayes' name at Ohio Stadium.

After unveiling the banner behind a sweater vest-themed cover in honor of Tressel's signature outfit, Tressel spoke about the honor.

"This recognition, it's about these young men," Tressel said, pointing to a crowd of his former players. "These great coaches, these great fans, The Best Damn Band in the Land and everyone that loves the Buckeyes. I thank God every day; he made me a Buckeye."

Tressel joins Paul Brown and Hayes as the only coaches so honored at the stadium. Their names are fixed in the southeast corner of the stadium's C Deck.

He's also the first addition to the Ring of Honor at Ohio Stadium since former Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Troy Smith in 2014.

Tressel, who serves as Ohio's lieutenant governor, coached the Buckeyes for 10 seasons and led them to a BCS national championship in 2002, a breakthrough for a program that had gone more than three decades without winning a title.

articles.title: Former NFL lineman has major concerns about Steelers’ new-look O-line
articles.summary: Could a new scheme hurt the development of the Steelers’ young offensive line?
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering the 2026 season with a revamped offensive line and a new offensive philosophy under head coach Mike McCarthy. According to former NFL center A.Q. Shipley, the transition could create some significant problems.

Shipley, who spent 12 seasons in the NFL, joined The Pat McAfee Show this week to discuss Pittsburgh's offensive line and expressed concern about how the group will adapt to McCarthy's system.

"I'm concerned about the Steelers offensive line," he said. "I think they're going to take a step back."

Shipley believes the issue goes beyond individual talent. Instead, he pointed to the schematic transition from former offensive coordinator Arthur Smith to McCarthy as a potentially significant challenge.

"Scheme and fit are everything," he said. "I think they were built to run in Arthur Smith's wide-zone scheme, and now Mike McCarthy is a more pro-style, downhill, gap-scheme."

That change could be particularly important for a young offensive line that was beginning to develop familiarity with Smith's system. McCarthy, who is also calling the plays in Pittsburgh, has brought a different offensive philosophy with him, including a greater emphasis on power/gap concepts and physicality up front.

The Steelers have also undergone considerable personnel changes along the line.

Zach Frazier remains the anchor at center after establishing himself as one of the league's better young centers. Troy Fautanu is taking over at left tackle, while Mason McCormick has moved to left guard. Rookie Max Iheanachor is also in the mix on the right side, but Dylan Cook will likely start the season at right tackle.

The Steelers recently traded former first-round pick Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys, further changing the complexion of the unit heading into the regular season.

That leaves Pittsburgh with a group featuring plenty of youth and athleticism, but also a significant amount of responsibility in a new system.

Shipley believes that transition could expose the Steelers, particularly if the offensive line struggles to generate the necessary movement in a more physical scheme.

"I think they struggled handling that a little bit," he said.

There are reasons for optimism, however. The Steelers have spent plenty of draft capital in the group in recent seasons, with Frazier and Fautanu establishing themselves as foundational players for the future.

Still, Shipley's pessimism highlights one of the biggest questions surrounding Pittsburgh entering the McCarthy era: Can a young offensive line quickly adjust to a completely different offensive identity? The group's rough preseason didn't do much to alleviate those concerns

With Aaron Rodgers entering the season behind center and Pittsburgh hoping to compete immediately, the answer could have a major impact on how successful the new-look offense becomes.

articles.title: Serie A | Inter 3-2 Napoli: Lautaro Martinez seals thrilling comeback victory
articles.summary: Inter completed an extraordinary comeback from 2-0 down to beat Napoli 3-2 with a Lautaro Martinez double and Marcus Thuram, sealing a true thriller at San S...
articles.body:
Inter completed an extraordinary comeback from 2-0 down to beat Napoli 3-2 with a Lautaro Martinez double and Marcus Thuram, sealing a true thriller at San Siro.

The top two in each of the last two seasons faced off , though the Nerazzurri had started stronger with victories over Monza and Cagliari. Marcus Thuram was still not fully fit and Djed Spence working his way back from injury, with John Stones and Hakan Calhanoglu rested ahead of the Champions League trip to Real Madrid.

Max Allegri had a rough week, losing at home to Como, then Scott McTominay and Giovane both required surgery , with Alessandro Buongiorno and Luca Marianucci already long-term absentees. Antonio Vergara was preferred to Kevin De Bruyne due to match fitness.

Napoli were unbeaten against Inter since the Supercoppa Italiana Final in January 2024, managing one win and four draws going into this test.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, gestures during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Alex Meret got down to palm an Andy Diouf first-time finish round the base of the near post from the edge of the area in the opening 70 seconds.

Josep Martinez also showed remarkable reflexes to deny Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa from close range on the Alisson Santos roll across from the left, also parrying the Matteo Politano follow-up.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Antonio Vergara of Napoli is challenged by Piotr Zielinski of Internazionale during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Manuel Akanji deflected the Anguissa first-time strike onto the side-netting, while Yann Bisseck fired just over shrugging off Rafa Marin inside the penalty area.

Rasmus Hojlund didn't get enough power behind the finish at the back stick from a flicked-on corner, allowing Josep Martinez to make the save, while it was tougher for Meret to deny Lautaro Martinez after good work from Federico Dimarco.

In the last kick of the first half, Dimarco bent a free kick over the wall and smacked it against the crossbar at the near top corner.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Alisson Santos of Napoli is challenged by Nicolo Barella of Internazionale during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Curtis Jones and Marcus Thuram came on for the second half, while Inter had penalty appeals rejected for potential Lobotka handling offence that bounced off Barella's chest.

Moments later, Inter made a mess playing out from the back with Barella, so Josep Martinez denied Alisson Santos and Barella charged down the first Politano strike, but the follow-up arrowed through a sea of legs into the net.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Matteo Politano of Napoli celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Meret flew to palm a ferocious Piotr Zielinski half-volley out from under the bar, but Napoli doubled their lead in chaotic circumstances.

After Josep Martinez got his glove to another Alisson Santos effort, the clearance didn't go out of play, so Giovanni Di Lorenzo put it back in for Hojlund's snooker shot through a sea of legs into the far bottom corner from the edge of the area with the inside of the left boot, catching Inter napping.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Rasmus Hojlund of Napoli celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

The hosts got back into it, as Dimarco volleyed down a Zielinski cross at the by-line for Lautaro Martinez to come sliding in from six yards, anticipating Amir Rrahmani.

Lautaro Martinez couldn't control another Dimarco assist, while Marcus Thuram was unlucky to see his header bounce off the upright on 73 minutes.

It was only a warning, as Thuram did nod in the equaliser from a Carlos Augusto cross into the near bottom corner, beating debutant Benoit Badiashile in the air. Napoli weren't happy, as Amir Rrahmani was on the ground in the six-yard box.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Marcus Thuram of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

The game was wide open, as Thuram first and then David Neres fired over from incredibly promising positions, while Anguissa somehow failed to keep his finish on target when trying to redirect the Lorenzo Lucca wayward volley.

It proved costly, as when Barella's effort was palmed over the bar, the resulting corner wasn't cleared effectively, Manuel Akanji prodded it away from Meret for Lautaro Martinez to bundle over the line from a couple of yards.

articles.title: Alexandra Eala Predicted to Fall to Iva Jovic at US Open as Former Pros Point to American’s Technical Edge
articles.summary: The third-round clash between 18-year-old Iva Jovic and 21-year-old Alexandra Eala at the US Open is set to be an intriguing matchup. While the night session...
articles.body:
The third-round clash between 18-year-old Iva Jovic and 21-year-old Alexandra Eala at the US Open is set to be an intriguing matchup. While the night session will feature two of the WTA's rising stars and close friends battling for a spot in the second week, analysts have weighed in on who holds the edge based on their recent form and head-to-head record.

Alexandra Eala's US Open Run Faces Tough Iva Jovic Test After American Dominated First Two Meetings

The Filipina comes into New York with plenty of confidence after her breakthrough title run at the DC Open, while Jovic struggled, suffering early exits in both Canada and Cincinnati.

However, Jovic has a 2-0 head-to-head record against Eala, with the American winning in straight sets in their last official match at the HSBC Championships during grass-court season.

On Tennis Channel, former World No. 1 Lindsay Davenport and ATP pro-turned-analyst Prakash Amritraj have both pointed out the two players' different styles.

"It'll be an interesting matchup," Davenport observed . "Jovic has dominated their previous two matches, but much different momentum coming in here. Eala was the much better player on the hard courts over the summer… So, she comes in with maybe a little bit of a different mindset."

Despite Eala's strong summer form, Davenport highlighted Jovic's aggressive baseline game as a major challenge. Jovic plays close to the baseline and takes the ball very early, giving opponents little time to react. Eala will have to work hard in defense to handle her heavy pace and early ball-striking.

Amritraj picked the World No. 14 based on her overall game, while also acknowledging Eala's advantage in the current conditions.

"I lean towards Jovic, not just because of the history," Amritraj explained. "This, of course, is on the hard court, but I just feel she's a better player at the moment."

However, he also admitted that Eala's recent success makes her a serious threat, noting that the hard courts suit Eala's rhythm.

Meanwhile, Jovic and Eala's friendship adds another interesting angle. Their close bond began in 2022, when Eala won the US Open girls' title.

Recently, they played an exhibition match as part of the "Stars of the Open" event during the Fan Week at the US Open, where Jovic won. They also surprised fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium by bringing their fathers onto the court for a fun doubles rally.

Now, both players know they will have to put their friendship aside once they step onto the court.

"Obviously, it's very difficult to be friends and also compete," Jovic explained after her second-round win. "But then, on the court, it's fair game, winner takes all; we go for it. Alex is definitely one of those people where we both put it aside."

Eala shared the same view. "Iva, yes, she's an amazing player. Young, very talented, and very intelligent," Eala noted during her presser. "I've encountered my fair share of challenges against her this year. All I can do is give my best and try to do everything that I can to win."

Their third-round match is scheduled at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Could Alabama Standout Ryan Coleman-Williams Be Dealing With ‘The Yips’?
articles.summary: Ryan Coleman-Williams had two baffling drops in Alabama's Week 1 opener. Can the talented junior wideout finally take the leap the Crimson Tide expect?
articles.body: Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams — Ryan Williams at the time — put together a freshman season that made college football fans believe he had the goods to be the next great Crimson Tide pass-catcher. Coleman-Williams kicked off his college career with a bang, hauling in two catches for 139 yards — both of which went for touchdowns — in Alabama's 2024 season-opening win over Western Kentucky. At just 17 years old, one of the youngest players in FBS football, he appeared to be heading for superstardom. The 6-foot, 184-pound wideout put together massive outings against the likes of Vanderbilt, Georgia and Tennessee, concluding his true freshman season with 48 catches for 865 yards and 10 total touchdowns. He earned first-team All-SEC and second-team All-American honors while also being named a freshman All-American. Last year, though, was another story. Coleman-Williams failed to take the next step many expected him to take, despite playing with an elite-level quarterback in Ty Simpson, who went on to be selected in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft by the Los Angeles Rams. Now, with sophomore Keelon Russell under center and another offseason under his belt, this is supposed to be the year Coleman-Williams takes his game to another level. But early indications show Coleman-Williams still has a few things to work out before he's ready to reach that superstar level. In Alabama's Week 1 opener, Coleman-Williams had a pair of inexplicable drops, leaving fans to wonder: Is the junior wideout dealing with a case of the "yips?" The first drop came midway through the opening quarter when Russell found Coleman-Williams wide open down the seam. The junior leaped for the catch, but the ball fell right through his hands. "That’s the bugaboo from last season," the broadcast crew said following the unexplainable drop. Later in the half, as Alabama was driving down the field, Coleman-Williams ran a fade-stop route and Russell found him open in the end zone. Yet again, though, the ball went right through his hands. Coleman-Williams did make up for it, finishing the opening half with four catches for 100 yards. For Coleman-Williams, the drops were impossible to ignore, particularly given the expectations surrounding him entering his junior season, but his four catches for 100 yards in the first half also offered a reminder of the playmaking ability that made him such a highly touted prospect when he arrived in Tuscaloosa. One game isn't everything, but if the Crimson Tide are going to make a run at a national title this season, they'll need their star wideout to turn those flashes of brilliance into consistency.

articles.title: Liverpool Are Big Admirers Of This Wolves Winger: Should Iraola Move In For Him In January?
articles.summary: In a recent report, journalist Graeme Bailey claimed that Liverpool are big admirers of Wolverhampton Wanderers winger Mateus Mane. It has been mentioned tha...
articles.body:
In a recent report , journalist Graeme Bailey claimed that Liverpool are big admirers of Wolverhampton Wanderers winger Mateus Mane. It has been mentioned that the Reds could face competition from Manchester United in pursuit of the Portuguese youngster.

Mane's Impressive Rise In English Football

Mane managed to catch the eye at times for Wolves in the Premier League last season when he put in a string of impressive displays for them in the final third. The 18-year-old found the back of the net three times and earned a couple of assists in 27 matches for the West Midlands club in the league.

The talented teenager is currently among the most gifted wide players in his homeland. Hence, it is no surprise that the Reds are among the clubs keeping tabs on him.

His current contract at the Midlands club will run out in the summer of 2029, which could make it tough for Liverpool to land him on a cut-price deal next year.

WOLVERHAMPTON, ENGLAND – AUGUST 07: Mateus Mane of Wolverhampton Wanderers runs with the ball during the Carabao Cup first round match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Port Vale at Molineux on August 07, 2026 in Wolverhampton, England. (Photo by David Rogers/Getty Images)

Should Liverpool Boss Andoni Iraola Move In For Mane In January?

Mane is proficient at creating some space for himself to get some strikes in at goal. He has the vision to engineer some promising chances for his teammates in the final third and is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet.

The Portuguese talent can even chip in by scoring and creating a few important goals for his team from the wide areas. Mane is primarily a left-winger but can also serve a central striker or play in the number ten position if needed. He is already quite familiar with the Premier League and won't take much time to adjust to life at the Merseyside club.

We can expect Mane to bring more firepower to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's attack. He has what it takes to serve as a good rotational piece in the Merseyside club's squad.

At 18, the future looks quite promising for Mane as long as he continues to improve with each season. He is undoubtedly a prospect to watch out for in the long run, so Iraola would be wise to move in for him when the transfer window reopens in January, but only if he is available for a reasonable fee.

articles.title: Lakers legend gives thoughts on LeBron James joining Sixers on a deal
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers legend Derek Fisher gives his thoughts on LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers on a deal.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers were able to win the offseason with the moves they were able to make to improve the roster. President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey and the staff were able to land the likes of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James in an effort to seriously challenge in the Eastern Conference.

The acquisition of Brown from the Boston Celtics set up the move to land James in free agency. The future Hall of Famer joins Philadelphia after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers and will be looking to help the Sixers end a long title drought as the franchise has not won a title since 1983.

Lakers legend Derek Fisher spoke on James joining the Sixers, per Yahoo! Sports :

"I like the move on just pure basketball based on where LeBron is as a veteran player," Fisher said. "He gets labelled a lot for being very self-absorbed while he's typically made a lot of basketball decisions that are about team success. "He's chasing winning, which is a team thing. Yes, it would positively add to his individual legacy to be a part of another team that plays in the NBA Finals, which I think the Sixers have a chance to get to. "So I like the move in terms of, at this age and where he is in his journey, there's no reason for him to have to be the best player on the team. Shouldn't even try to be the best player on the team."

James averaged 20.9 points per game with the Lakers in 2025-26, and to Fisher's point, he won't have to be the best player on the Sixers every night. As Philadelphia moves forward, it will need James to produce, but the scoring responsibilities will be placed upon Brown, Joel Embiid, and Tyrese Maxey. It's a perect fit.
