articles.title: Steelers 'likely' plan with Drew Allar in rookie season revealed by ESPN insider
articles.summary: The plan for the Steelers' rookie QB is not a good one for opportunity in 2026.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have Aaron Rodgers as their starting quarterback for the 2026 NFL season, in what's set to be the last of a Hall of Fame NFL career.

But after him on the depth chart are three other quarterbacks. Mason Rudolph is the backup, while Will Howard and Drew Allar are the developmental quarterback projects.

With four QBs on the roster, it's fair to wonder what the plan is for Allar in his rookie season. Well, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano , their most likely plan is not a good one for Allar to see the field in 2026.

Steelers likely to make Drew Allar decision that some fans might not like

"But Allar feels less likely to play this season than Beck or Klubbnik," Graziano writes. "... we can't rule out Allar starting in a tryout-type role if Pittsburgh's season collapses, but it usually does not."

The Steelers are going to be starting Rodgers all season in 2026, as they're likely going to be good enough to contend for the playoffs.

In his last year, the Steelers are not likely to bench Rodgers. So, it would likely take an injury to Rodgers or some extreme circumstances to force a QB change.

One of those extreme outcomes could come in the form of the Steelers either securing a playoff spot before Week 18 and deciding to rest Rodgers for the first round of the playoffs.

Allar then could get a chance to start. However, with Rudolph and Howard also potential options to start for the Steelers, Allar's odds of being a starter this year aren't great.

The former Penn State quarterback is more likely to sit on the bench all season, learn from Rodgers, and go into 2027 training camp and preseason with a real chance to win the QB1 job.

Whether it's competing solely against Howard, or with a new rookie quarterback, free agent pickup, or trade addition, the Steelers' QB competition next summer is going to be one to watch.

But, at least for the 2026 NFL season, and Allar's rookie year, it's likely that the Steelers won't send out the Penn State rookie at any point this season.

articles.title: India crush Pakistan at T20 Asia Cup with record-breaking bowling display
articles.summary: India claim seven-wicket win after Pakistan lose 10 wickets for just 28 runs as they are bowled out for 55.
articles.body:
India produced a dominant display to defeat Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai, bowling their rivals out for their lowest total in the format before rattling off their target inside nine overs.

Pakistan, having won the toss and elected to bat at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday, made a promising start but collapsed spectacularly after an opening partnership of 27.

India eventually dismissed them for just 55 in 18.1 overs, with their spinners responsible for much of the damage.

Shree Charani and Prema Rawat were the stars of the bowling attack, taking three wickets apiece. Charani finished with remarkable figures of 3 for 7 from four overs, while Rawat returned 3 for 9. Deepti Sharma added two wickets for only five runs.

Pakistan’s innings initially appeared under control. Muneeba Ali made 13, and Shawaal Zulfiqar scored 14 for the first wicket.

But Shafali Verma broke the partnership by bowling Muneeba, and Charani then struck twice in the sixth over. She dismissed Gull Feroza for a duck before removing Zulfiqar, leaving Pakistan 29 for three.

The collapse continued almost immediately as Pakistan slipped to 32 for four in the eighth over before Rawat and Deepti Sharma intensified the pressure. By the 13th over, Pakistan were 45 for seven, and there was no prospect of recovering to a competitive total.

The final three wickets eventually fell with Pakistan on 55, giving India an exceptionally modest target. The total was Pakistan’s lowest in women’s T20I cricket, surpassing their previous low of 63 against India in the 2012 Women’s Twenty20 Asia Cup.

Despite requiring only 56, India did not have everything their own way at the start of the chase.

Pakistan’s bowlers claimed three wickets, giving their opponents a brief glimpse of an unlikely route back into the contest. Fatima Sana was Pakistan’s most successful bowler, finishing with 3 for 17.

The target, however, was simply too small. India reached 57 for three in 8.4 overs, completing a seven-wicket victory with Harmanpreet Kaur unbeaten on 18. The Indian captain ensured there was no late drama and guided her side across the line with plenty of deliveries to spare.

The victory maintained India’s perfect start to the tournament. They now have six points from three matches and have already secured their place in the semifinals.

For Pakistan, meanwhile, the defeat leaves their qualification hopes dependent on their final group match against Hong Kong. They remain on two points and need a victory to give themselves a chance of progressing.

articles.title: Atalanta ‘need time’ to adapt with Sarri, possible Rowe and Kessie debut
articles.summary: Atalanta director of sport Cristiano Giuntoli admits ‘it will take time’ to adapt with Maurizio Sarri’s tactics, but Franck Kessié and Jonathan Rowe could de...
articles.body:
Atalanta director of sport Cristiano Giuntoli admits 'it will take time' to adapt with Maurizio Sarri's tactics, but Franck Kessié and Jonathan Rowe could debut against Roma.

It kicks off at the Stadio Olimpico at 19.45 UK time (20.45 CEST).

La Dea scraped late victories against Sassuolo and Bologna, as well as securing their place in the Conference League by beating Hapoel Tel-Aviv in the play-offs.

Jonathan Rowe signs the Atalanta contract alongside director Cristiano Giuntoli, completing his move from Bologna (atalanta.it)

"I hope it will be a great game and an advertisement for football. These are teams with completely different tactical concepts, but both aiming for success, so we'll see what happens," Giuntoli told Sky Sport Italia.

Kamaldeen Sulemana and Isak Hien are still on the treatment table, but the squad has been bolstered on deadline day by Rowe from Bologna at €40m plus add-ons, and the return to Bergamo of free agent Kessié.

Franck Kessie signs the contract alongside Atalanta directors Cristiano Giuntoli and Luca Percassi (atalanta.it)

"Franck made the choice with his heart, the rapport with Luca Percassi was decisive, and he embraced our project. We think Rowe can give us the quality in the final third that we are looking for."

Atalanta had spent nine years under current Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini, but decided to go in a very different direction with Sarri this time.

BERGAMO, ITALY – AUGUST 31: Maurizio Sarri, Head Coach of Atalanta reacts during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Bologna FC at Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia on August 31, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

"We believe it takes time, because we are changing from man-marking to zonal, so that is a completely different way of looking at football. The lads need to adapt, it will take a while, but we are confident that we can do well.

"We trust that we did some good things on the transfer market, and we'll have to show it on the field," concluded Giuntoli.

articles.title: Así era la lujosa vida de alias 'Bendito Menor', el narcoinfluencer abatido en Colombia
articles.standfirst: De presumir lujos y burlarse del Gobierno a caer abatido
articles.summary: De presumir lujos y burlarse del Gobierno a caer abatido
articles.body: En una operación silenciosa y sigilosa llevada a cabo por la Policía Nacional en la madrugada del 4 de septiembre de 2026, fue abatido Naín Andrés Pérez Toncel, alias 'Naín' o 'Bendito Menor', señalado como máximo líder del Frente Javier Cáceres de las Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada (ACSN), también conocidas como 'Los Pachenca'. El operativo se desarrolló en una vivienda ubicada en el barrio Los Olivos, en las inmediaciones del aeropuerto de Riohacha, en el departamento de La Guajira. En el procedimiento también perdieron la vida su pareja sentimental, Rosa Angélica Tarazona —conocida como alias 'La Bebecita', quien lo acompañaba en sus actividades delictivas— y dos de sus escoltas. Alias 'Bendito Menor', de 26 años, representaba una amenaza prioritaria para la seguridad del Caribe colombiano. Su injerencia delictiva abarcaba no solo el departamento de La Guajira, sino también Cesar, Magdalena y las estribaciones de la Sierra Nevada, donde delinquía a través del narcotráfico, la extorsión y la intimidación a la población. Debido al peligro que representaba, las autoridades ofrecían una recompensa de hasta $1.000 millones por información que permitiera su captura. Lejos del perfil tradicional y clandestino de los grandes cabecillas criminales, Pérez Toncel adoptó un estilo de vida mediático. Con una actitud desafiante y retadora, se movilizaba en motocicletas de alto cilindraje y utilizaba las redes sociales para presumir lujos, grandes sumas de dinero en efectivo y mansiones. En plataformas digitales acumulaba miles de seguidores y publicaba contenidos junto a su pareja en los que abiertamente se burlaba de las instituciones y de las medidas gubernamentales. Incluso, cuando se oficializó la millonaria recompensa por su cabeza, el cabecilla grabó videos mofándose públicamente de la decisión oficial y asegurando que se encontraba "relajadito" recorriendo los rincones de La Guajira. Aunque su cuenta de TikTok fue eliminada posteriormente por las políticas de la plataforma frente al crimen organizado, su presencia digital era constante. Su vida privada también formaba parte del espectáculo digital. Pocos días antes de ser abatido, protagonizó un ostentoso compromiso romántico con su pareja sentimental, Rosa Angélica Tarazona, alias ‘La Bebecita’ (quien también murió en el mismo procedimiento táctico). Dicha pedida de mano incluyó un camino de rosas y antorchas encendidas a la orilla del mar, imágenes que rápidamente circularon y alimentaron su estatus de figura intocable ante los ojos de sus seguidores. El punto de quiebre en la persecución contra ‘Bendito Menor’ ocurrió cuando las autoridades decidieron fijar una millonaria recompensa de hasta 1.000 millones de pesos por información que permitiera su captura, declarándolo de manera oficial como un objetivo de alto valor estratégico. Lejos de resguardarse, el cabecilla respondió con mofas y provocaciones públicas. A través de un video difundido masivamente, se burló de la medida gubernamental mientras realizaba recorridos campantes por corregimientos como El Dividivi, en jurisdicción de Riohacha. “Conquistador hasta la muerte. Estamos aquí, ve. $1.000 millones dando vueltas, relajaitos. Estamos es sorneados, papi, sornerito. En todos los rincones de la Guajira, mira, ve... para que digan que es con la IA ahora. No, eso es nítido”, vociferaba de manera desafiante en la grabación, mofándose incluso de la tecnología de inteligencia artificial utilizada en labores de inteligencia militar. Asimismo, las ACSN intentaron legitimar su presencia criminal en la zona mediante discursos populistas armados en los que prometían cesar cobros a pequeños comerciantes, mientras circulaban registros gráficos donde su propio anillo de seguridad cruzaba armado puestos de control militar sin oposición aparente, avivando la sensación de impunidad que rodeaba al grupo armado. La altanería digital y las caravanas desafiantes protagonizadas por el grupo armado en julio de ese año agotaron la paciencia del Gobierno Nacional. Con la directriz clara del presidente de la República, Abelardo de la Espriella, de catalogarlo como un "miserable" e implementar una postura implacable contra los actores armados que rehusaran el sometimiento a la justicia, las capacidades técnicas y de inteligencia del Estado —con apoyo tecnológico especializado— se volcaron sobre el norte del país. El operativo final desmanteló el núcleo del Frente Javier Cáceres. Junto a ‘Bendito Menor’ y su pareja ‘La Bebecita’, cayeron abatidos dos de sus hombres de confianza más cercanos: alias ‘El Tío’, señalado como cabecilla logístico, y alias ‘Casiloco’, encargado del componente financiero de la estructura criminal. La muerte de Naín Andrés Pérez Toncel envía un mensaje contundente sobre el fin de la era en la que cabecillas del narcotráfico y el paramilitarismo creían poder desafiar a las instituciones parapetados tras la pantallas de los teléfonos móviles y el dinero ilícito. La ostentación digital de ‘Bendito Menor’ terminó por facilitarle las coordenadas a la inteligencia estatal, convirtiendo su fugaz paso como "narcoinfluencer" en un recordatorio de que el margen de maniobra para los criminales de alto valor es cada vez más estrecho.

articles.title: LSU leaves former pros Wright and Harris off opening day roster
articles.summary: LSU did not place onetime pros Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on its roster in advance of its season opener.
articles.body: LSU did not place onetime pros Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on its roster in advance of its season opener. The move appears to avoid an immediate confrontation with the Southeastern Conference, which had passed a rule forbidding former pros on rosters only to see that rule put on hold by a court in Louisiana. It means LSU will open its season against Clemson on Saturday night without Wright and Harris — each of whom spent time in NFL training camps this summer. “That wasn’t easy,” coach Lane Kiffin said Saturday on ESPN’s “College GameDay.” “As much as I feel for the players, and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe these kids have an opportunity to play just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters. “But at the same time, I’m the head coach of LSU, and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster. We couldn’t get exact reasons or exact what that would mean if we added them. So with that, we made the decision which is in the best interest of the team and the university.” Both Wright and Harris have said they are enrolled at LSU, which means they could be eligible to be added to the roster later. Legal action is ongoing, with the SEC planning an appeal of the Louisiana ruling and also awaiting word on a federal lawsuit it filed Thursday asking the court to force LSU into following its rules banning pro athletes. The roster decision marked the latest move in a bizarre, wide-ranging disagreement over something most people used to agree on: that players who had moved on to pro sports from college could not return to college. Under the rules the SEC passed last week that were subsequently shut down by the Louisiana court, the league could suspend coach Lane Kiffin, fine LSU half its football budget and more if it puts Wright and Harris on the roster. The case stems from a new NCAA rule that granted five seasons of eligibility for players who started college in 2023. Wright, Harris and dozens of others across the country who started in 2022 have filed lawsuits saying they also deserve a fifth year of eligibility. Embedded within that argument is whether players among that class who tried out for NFL, NBA or WNBA teams should be able to come back to college and play. “The SEC’s presidents and chancellors unanimously adopted a clear and reasonable standard: Member universities should not place former professional athletes on their rosters,” the conference said in a statement after Thursday night’s loss in Louisiana court. In its own statement Friday, LSU said it was reviewing the court’s order and would “continue to work constructively with the SEC and NCAA as this matter moves forward.” Also chiming in was the College Football Playoff, which came out in support of the rules barring former pros from the college gridiron. It wasn’t a surprising stance, considering virtually all of CFP management is made up of the same school leaders who adopted the rules. Meanwhile, the LSU decision came hours after Clemson general counsel Chip Hood sent a letter to his LSU counterpart suggesting the eligibility issue is in conflict with the contract between the teams to play. Clemson still plans to show up, though its coach, Dabo Swinney, left little doubt over his feelings earlier in the week. “I would just say it’s kind of embarrassing,” he said. “I mean, honestly, it’s just embarrassing that that’s where we are. I don’t blame the kids and people trying to take advantage of the system. I just think it’s embarrassing where we are with college football.”

articles.title: Everton vs Manchester United: Premier League – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Manchester United outspent in transfer window, but boss Michael Carrick says team ready to fire ahead of Everton trip.
articles.body:
Who: Everton vs Manchester United What: English Premier League Where: Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom When: Sunday, August 6, at 2pm (13:00 GMT). How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 10:00 GMT ahead of our live coverage.

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said he is delighted with the additions to his squad despite being outspent by Premier League rivals in the transfer window and short on depth in some areas.

United put their efforts into rebuilding Carrick’s midfield , with Casemiro’s exit and a serious injury to Manuel Ugarte offset by the acquisitions of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba for a combined 155 million pounds ($210m).

The Red Devils’ fiercest rivals spent almost that budget on a single player as Manchester City broke the British transfer record for Enzo Fernandez , while Liverpool splashed up to 123 million pounds ($166m) on French winger Bradley Barcola .

Despite returning to the Champions League for the first time in three seasons, Carrick hinted at having to work within financial restrictions.

“We went into the window wanting to come out stronger from the group that we had last season. We’ve definitely added to that,” Carrick told a pre-match media conference ahead of Sunday’s trip to Everton.

“I think we’ve done a lot of good work in that respect and the situation is what it is in terms of finances and what we can work with and what we’re trying to get the most of.

“Certainly, the players that we’ve brought into the group I’m absolutely delighted with and I think we’ve done some really good business there.”

What areas of doubt remain for Manchester United?

United look particularly short in defence with the injury-prone Luke Shaw their only senior option at left-back.

“What squad ever is the perfect squad? You’ve always got to find ways of adapting,” Carrick added.

“When you’re building and trying to push to go through a period where we’re trying to get to the top – that’s the ultimate goal – you’ve got to make steps.”

Joshua Zirkzee was among those expected to leave Old Trafford to boost the funds available to Carrick.

Despite interest from Fiorentina and Juventus and a deadline-day approach from Everton, the Netherlands international remains at United, despite limited game time over the past two seasons.

“He wants to play more than he has done and that’s the good competition and healthy competition for places,” said Carrick.

“Josh can do some really, really top things. I’ve seen it myself, and I know he can do that and looking forward to him doing that a little bit more often for us.”

How have Manchester United started the Premier League season?

After a dreadful 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United bounced back to thrash Ipswich 5-2 thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick last time out.

Everton boss David Moyes conceded ‌he is left with a small squad after a disappointing transfer window in ⁠which key players departed ⁠and a deadline day medical fell through as they tried to sign American striker Folarin Balogun.

Moyes expressed frustration at his club’s close-season business , ⁠revealing they did not want to lose Senegal forward Iliman Ndiaye but were powerless when bigger teams like Manchester City look to sign their players.

“Disappointed we didn’t do more business ⁠and disappointed things didn’t go our way in the end. Sometimes in football you have to live with disappointment and we will move on,” Moyes told reporters on Friday.

“I know what I needed and I know what it’s like to build a squad for the Premier League, I know ‌the numbers you need. I’ve been around long enough to know that, but some things went against us and some things could have gone better.

“Ultimately, we didn’t want to lose a lot of the players, but for different reasons that had to happen.”

AS Monaco chief executive Thiago Scuro said Everton raised concerns over Balogun’s medical late on deadline day and that the US international pulled out because he was uncomfortable with the doubts ⁠raised by the Merseyside club over his health.

“It wasn’t anybody’s fault. ⁠It happens in football a lot,” Moyes said.

“The player had a problem in his medical and that was simply it. There’s no other story behind it.”

Everton face fans backlash over transfer window business

Everton’s Fans’ Forum also criticised the club’s planning and recruitment after the transfer ⁠window closed, saying supporters deserved answers after another window marked by late activity and a failed pursuit of key targets.

With a thin ⁠squad, Moyes said Everton’s academy players would have to step ⁠up but was unsure if they could fill the gaps.

“Are they ready to make the step up? I’m not sure about that. We will see how that goes, some of them might be pushed in,” Moyes said.

“They’re all ‌going to have to be able to muck in as we’ve got a real small squad now,” he added.

“It gives opportunities to some people who have not had them and sometimes ‌in ‌football you need to be given that chance so that you can show what you can do. Let’s see if some of them can do that.”

What happened the last time Everton faced Manchester United?

Manchester United were 1-0 winners in the last meeting of the sides, which came in a Premier League fixture at Hill Dickinson Stadium in February.

Benjamin Sesko scored the only goal after 71 minutes.

When did Everton last beat Manchester United?

Everton won 1-0 in the Premier League fixture at Old Trafford last season – despite being reduced to ten men early on.

Idrissa Gueye was sent off in the 14th minute, while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall came up with what would be the winner on the halfway mark.

Prediction – Everton vs Manchester United

The Opta supercomputer is giving Everton a 38.3 percent chance of winning, while offering United only a 33.3 percent chance of claiming the spoils.

This will be their 216th meeting with United winning 97 times and Everton 69.

The first meeting came in 1892 with Everton winning the English top flight encounter 6-0. The Toffees hit 10 against United that season as they completed the double with a 4-3 away win.

Jack Grealish is set to come straight into the matchday squad following his transfer deadline day loan from Manchester City.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles could also appear following the September 1 move for the ex-Arsenal defender. Christian Norgaard, another former Gunner, misses out with a knock.

Pickford; O’Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, Grealish; Barry

Carlos Baleba’s ankle continues to prevent his United debut. Manuel Ugarte, Amad Diallo and Matthijs de Ligt are all injured.

Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Tom Heaton all face late fitness tests.

Manchester United predicted starting lineup

articles.title: Leeds Rhinos 8-40 Wigan Warriors: Matt Peet's side close in on domestic double with statement win over Leeds
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors now take top spot off Leeds Rhinos with one round remaining; A win in Round 27 will give Wigan their second trophy of the year; The regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Warriors climbed above the Rhinos heading into the final round, with a victory at home to Catalans Dragons next week enough to secure them the League Leaders' Shield.

As for Leeds Rhinos, they must now beat Hull FC and hope the Warriors lose to the Dragons, otherwise they will have to settle for second place, despite holding top spot for several months.

Bevan French was the star as he produced two sublime assists and scored a try, with Adam Keighran scoring a hat-trick on an evening when Leeds were badly hampered by the early withdrawal of Lachie Miller, who was forced off with a hamstring injury inside seven minutes.

Keighran scored twice in the five minutes after that, and while Leeds responded through Ash Handley, further tries through Austin Daniel, Liam Marshall, Jai Field and Keighran ensured it was Matt Peet's side who got the win.

Leeds given wake up call by Wigan with play-offs on the horizon

The first major moment of the game was arguably the most significant. Miller, a strong contender to land this year's Man of Steel, pulled up while returning a kick and signalled to the bench immediately to be brought off.

Within five minutes of that, Wigan had scored twice. Daniel, brought into the side after a calf injury to Jake Wardle in the week, showed great pace to burn Leeds down the touchline, and he passed in field for Keighran to score the first of a quickfire brace.

The centre missed the conversion but added the next one minutes later after crossing from a sublime Bevan French cut-out pass. That gave Wigan a 10-0 lead.

In need of a response, Leeds got one. After earning a penalty, Jake Connor put a blustering kick to the corner which Handley superbly caught before having the strength to crash over the line. Connor converted to leave Wigan four points ahead after a breathless quarter.

Leeds settled well after their score, but when you come up against French in this mood, there's little you can do. His next piece of brilliance was a joy to behold, cutting out three players with a bulled pass to find Daniel on the wing, who did the rest. Keighran converted again.

Connor tagged on a penalty goal in the final action before the break, but after half-time Wigan took control of the game.

Harry Smith's brilliant cut-out ball saw Leeds short and Zack Eckersley put Marshall over for a key score.

Leeds came close through Handley, who was only denied by a brilliant French try-saver, but the Warriors always appeared to have the Rhinos' number in defence, ending the game as comfortable winners.

Wigan wrapped it up with 14 minutes to play, French finishing a move from deep as Smith produced a superb reverse kick after spotting his halfback partner unmarked on the short side.

The Warriors made sure to go out in style. French produced a beautiful assist to send Field hurtling towards the line to score, before Keighran bagged his hat-trick in front of an electric Wigan faithful.

Partington: Wigan have one hand on League Leaders' Shield | Peet: We have shown consistency

Betfred Player of the Match Wigan Warriors' Oliver Partington speaking to Sky Sports:

"We've got a job to do next week against Catalans, so we're not looking past that, but it feels like we've got one hand on it (League Leaders' Shield).

"I think that's what Wigan fans pride themselves on from the top to the bottom is that effort on the field and not giving in.

"It was a massive game, it had that big-game feel, felt like a final and these are the games you want to play in, packed-out stadium, big event and credit to Leeds for putting it on."

On potential of Grand Final being between Wigan and Leeds: "We know we can do it, we've beat them twice now but I think they will be stinging and that will fuel them now this time of the season. It's probably the right time to lose and they can work on it. We're ready to face them but expect them to be better next time."

Wigan Warriors' head coach Matt Peet speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was good event, great crowd, good build-up. Probably a shame that Leeds lost Lachie Miller.

"I was happy with what my team did tonight very, very proud of them.

"It's a massive one for the club (the League Leaders' Shield). It says a lot about your consistency. To be consistent, a lot of people have got to do a good job, your academy has got to be well shaped, everyone's got to be fit and ready."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

The Hilltoppers (2-1) also made big plays defensively. Atticus Godfrey helped hold things together along the defensive line, keeping Kettle Moraine (0-3) from establishing its offense. Caleb Miller intercepted two passes for Marquette.

Kettle Moraine also generated turnovers, intercepting a pass to open the game and picking off another to start the second half. A late third-quarter, tip-drill interception added another momentum-changing play in a game that featured turnovers from both sides. Junior Jett Allen was a defensive leader for the Hilltoppers with 16 total tackles, including two tackles for loss, along with a fumble recovery.

Kettle Moraine was led offensively by senior Nico Yttre, who had 291 rushing yards and one touchdown.

articles.title: 76ers star LeBron James drops unexpected career announcement ahead of Year 24 kickoff
articles.summary: LeBron James has made another major announcement, and it has nothing to do with basketball. The 41-year-old revealed a new partnership with Polymarket on Sat...
articles.body:
LeBron James has made another major announcement, and it has nothing to do with basketball. The 41-year-old revealed a new partnership with Polymarket on Saturday morning.

It is the latest addition to a business portfolio that keeps growing alongside his playing career.

'Welcome to Polymarket HQ. Coming soon. In partnership with Polymarket,' James posted.

James adds another venture before his 24th season

The move surprised plenty of people, coming out of nowhere just days before his historic 24th NBA campaign begins in Philadelphia.

James had spent the whole summer as the biggest name on the market, finally deciding to join the 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal with a player option. It is a significant pay cut from the $50 million he earned with the Lakers last season.

He made his intentions clear in a series of social media posts announcing the move.

"This is my last decision. I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship," James wrote.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time."

The 76ers moved from 20-1 to 10-1 title odds after his arrival, joining him with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown.

James nearly walked away altogether. Swept from the playoffs in May, he admitted he thought he had played his final game.

"I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game," he said.

"I still truly love this game, and I have more to give."

That decision is Philadelphia's gain. The Polymarket news is just another sign that even at 41, the business side of LeBron never stops.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin’s Roster Decision Reverberates Across Baton Rouge
articles.summary: The legal battle over eligibility was ever-present in Death Valley on Saturday.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE — Lane Kiffin arrived on the set of ESPN's College GameDay around 10 a.m. local time with a look of determination. He still flashed a peace sign at LSU fans who cheered him as he walked, but otherwise didn't break stride.

Draped in a white button down and grey slacks, Kiffin was several hours away from making his debut as Tigers head coach. But first, he had some questions to answer about a massive and consequential decision.

On Friday night, LSU decided not to add Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to its final roster—a shocking turn after the players, as well as LSU itself, fought a legal battle for the right to take the field as Tigers.

Wright and Harris were just two of hundreds of college athletes who have sued the NCAA to challenge the implementation of its "age-based" eligibility policy , which offered a fifth year of eligibility to college athletes—but didn't include players from the freshman class of 2022 who had already completed, like them. But their lawsuit drew national news because they had signed NFL contracts, though both were waived before making regular-season roster. A multipart legal battle ensued after the SEC issued a ban on players with this NFL experience, and the players and LSU refused to back down.

In a Baton Rouge courthouse Thursday, players won an injunction to suit up Saturday—a court order that prevented both the NCAA and SEC from implementing its rules. During the nine-hour hearing—specifically when SEC commissioner Greg Sankey was on the stand—news broke that the conference had sued LSU in federal court in Alabama , adding another layer to the feud.

All day Friday, the college sports world waited with bated breath to see if Kiffin would test the limits of his fellow schools in the SEC, the NCAA, and even several politicians . Front Office Sports confirmed Friday night that Kiffin decided not to roster Wright and Harris. Attorney Darren Heitner, outside counsel for Wright's agent, later told FOS that Wright's representatives also received the news in the evening, but declined to comment further.

"LSU has made a measured decision to keep these two young men off the roster for now while preserving a place for them to be added later," Ryan Downton, an attorney representing the players, said in a statement Saturday. "Everyone should use that space to lower the temperature and look at the facts" that neither player was drafted, or made an NFL regular-season roster or practice squad.

By the time Saturday morning came, everyone was expecting an explanation from Kiffin as he took the GameDay stage. In front of hundreds of fans on the ESPN broadcast, he explained the decision "wasn't easy."

"As much as I feel for the players and I believe that you fight for what you believe in, and I believe these kids have an opportunity to play just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters," Kiffin added that "uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster" drove LSU to hold off.

Behind him, fans used the eligibility conundrum as just the latest example of a familiar narrative in Baton Rouge: that it is LSU vs. everyone; and now, LSU vs the SEC. One sign read: "My last sign was ruled ineligible." Another held up a split poster: One side depicted the SEC saying "see ya'll in court," while the other portrayed LSU saying, "see ya'll in Death Valley."

Even fans with a moral quandary about Kiffin's decision brought signs of support and cheered him on.

A trio of "lifelong" LSU fans from Lafayette held up one of the most colorful posters: A 13-year-old clutched a sign with the letters "SEC" spelling "Sankey Enjoys Court." The poster included what appeared to be an AI-generated image of Sankey kicked back at a desk wearing a purple suit and holding an alcoholic beverage. Matthew West, 50, standing beside him, said: "We thought that was hilarious because he [Sankey] was sitting in there, and then he filed that suit in Birmingham. We thought, 'Well man, he likes to be in court, apparently!"

Still, West, like some other LSU fans, doesn't necessarily think that Wright and Harris should set a new precedent. "I have a mixed opinion about that," he said. "It may be legal, but is it ethically clean for college football to have this happen? I don't know." He added, however, that he would have supported the players if they had been able to take the field.

Kiffin, for his part, was ushered off the GameDay set after the brief segment to head to a team meeting. Surrounded by body guards and athletic department officials, he put his game face back on and strode out of the limelight.

Later, another ESPN interview aired with Kiffin in that same outfit, expanding on his decision not to roster Wright and Harris. He suggested that he had concerns about potential postseason penalties, and also expressed remorse for his inability to support the two players who had attempted to follow him to LSU from Ole Miss (and NFL preseason).

Like LSU fans, Kiffin, too, is clinging to the LSU-vs.-everyone narrative.

"[The players] have a feeling… that they're treated different at LSU and have been treated different this week. And so that's probably a good thing," he said on ESPN. "That bonds people together, puts a little chip on their shoulder. And now they need to go play really well."
